verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The five inequalities are not stated as a list; the Lean fixes one uniform tolerance instead. `model_margins` takes delta from the Lipschitz estimate `model_estimate` and derives at line 770 the componentwise bound |observations(v,p) i - observations(0,p) i| ≤ m for every i : Fin 22, with m = min(1/5, e^{-8}/2) (line 760). Since e^{-8}/2 ≈ 1.68·10^{-4} < 1/5, m = e^{-8}/2, and two of the paper's five inequalities are available from that step. (i) a: the step `ha` at line 773 is |familyA F (v,p) - 4/5| ≤ m, i.e. |a - .8| ≤ 1.68·10^{-4}, which gives the paper's |a - .8| ≤ .1 about 600 times over; only the exported conclusion is the one-sided 3/5 ≤ a, obtained at line 782 through the weaker consequence hm1 : m ≤ 1/5 (line 779). (ii) b: `familyB_zero` (line 665) is b = 0 at the ideal control, so the same step at i = 19 reads |familyB F (v,p)| ≤ e^{-8}/2 — the proof instantiates only i = 18, 20, 21, but hcomp is universally quantified over i — and that gives the paper's |b_s| ≤ .1/(1+w_*) whenever 1 + w_* ≤ .2·e^8, i.e. for every w_* up to about 595; the Lean's b is the paper's -b_s (the sign convention of (4.11)) and both bounds are on absolute values, so the sign is immaterial. What is not stated is the other three: Q_s ≥ Q_min/2, E ≥ e_*/2 and |N_s/(EQ_s)| ≤ w_*. E (i=0), Q_s (i=16) and N_s (i=17) are controlled only through the same closeness-to-ideal bound, and the paper's constants Q_min, e_* and w_* = 1 + max|N_{s,0}/(E_0Q_{s,0})| have no Lean counterpart; the ratio N_s/(EQ_s) does occur in the repository (`OutgoingEntranceCone.directionRatio`, `HeatSwitchCone.familyB`) but not in the repair-stage tolerance. The paper's derived bounds v_s ≤ .9 + .01/.7 < 1 and the P_c floor appear instead as the two remaining exported margins familySpeed ≤ 1 and e^{-8}/2 ≤ familyProjection. The tolerance is fixed before the axis stage and its controls in both, and `exists_repair_cone` proves the relaxed cone on the restore/repair annulus, so the surrounding result is reached.
